This supports the conditional calculation, not the accuracy of the assumed costs or Google's estimated margin.
limitations: The evidence item contains an evaluator-derived calculation, not reported OpenAI financial results.
The sixfold cost assumption, baseline cost, and target margin are not independently validated.
The result is required revenue under the model, not necessarily a subscription price charged to each user.

statement.excerpt: That $32.5 is now $195. If it wanted to have the same margins, it would need to make $105 in profit from each user. So, $300. $300 a user for a product it hasn’t even built yet.

our_interpretation: This is a conditional arithmetic claim about the model presented on 2024-08-05, not an observation of SearchGPT's actual financial performance.
The supplied context makes the amounts annual dollars per user.
Margin means profit divided by revenue. The required revenue must leave 35% after the assumed costs.
The assumed cost, multiplier, and target margin are inputs to be tested for mathematical consistency, not independently established facts about either company.
The target period is the date of the stated calculation. No actual fiscal or calendar reporting year is assigned to the hypothetical annual amounts.
criteria.support_condition: The assumptions yield annual cost of $195 per user, required revenue of $300, and profit of $105, with profit equal to 35% of revenue.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Correct application of a 35% profit margin to the stated cost assumptions produces materially different figures.
